### Investment Memo: SE — 12 November 2026

**Verdict**: BUY — starter position only | Conviction: Low
**Price Target**: $86 (scenario-weighted; +17% from current $73.44)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
Sea is a genuinely high-quality operator — 44% LTM revenue growth, 45.9% gross margin, Rule of 40 of 56, net cash, no fraud signal — trading at the cheapest multiple in its history (1.18x EV/FY26E sales, ~16x FY27E EPS) after a 63% de-rating driven by margin timing and macro, not demand destruction. But the equity case is now hostage to one unfalsifiable variable: the loss rate on a $12.6B EM consumer-credit book (≈1:1 with book equity) where provisions have outgrown originations three consecutive quarters (+65% → +72% → +82% vs book +59%), with Q3 provisions ($682M) exceeding group operating income ($640M). Positive expected value, wide dispersion ($55–$135), hostile macro tape — this earns a small seat in the book, not a conviction position.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Macro UNFAVOURABLE — Fed hiking (90% priced for 9 Dec), USD +3.4%/8wks, IDR at record lows, BRL −10%/month; four of five channels adverse for a high-beta, USD-reporting EM lender. Offset: a December pause is a ~10:1 asymmetric event worth +30–45%. Sector NEUTRAL with company STRONG — 53% SEA GMV share, the only marketplace+logistics+payments+gaming integrated P&L, but TikTok Shop is forcing a spend war and Garena supplied ~54% of segment profit growth on just 5.9% bookings growth.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM. No sanctions exposure, no DOJ/SEC action, $46M class action settled and provisioned. But regulatory intensity is rising in every core profit pool — Indonesia (withholding agent role, KPPU precedent), Brazil (import-tax whipsaw), Vietnam (Decree 147), Taiwan (Garena concentration); Free Fire's 2022 India ban is the proven sovereign-removal template. Monee IPO adds disclosure surface.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: PASS at $73. Central IV $80–85 = only ~12% margin of safety vs a 25–30% requirement; a full buy needs $58–62. Headline 10% FCF yield is illusory — owner earnings are ~$1.44B (~3.2% yield) once the loan-book capital build is deducted; ROIC 11.7% ≈ WACC, not above it. Sea Cloud AI is a discipline red flag.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY. Revenue re-accelerating (43.4% Q3, 5.8% beat), gross margin +1,500bps since FY20, self-funding ($4.5B FY25 FCF, $9.5B gross cash). Withholds Strong Buy pending Shopee adj. EBITDA re-inflecting above ~$250M/quarter with GMV ≥25%.
- **Quantitative Signals**: NEUTRAL/underweight. Worst-in-peer-group on momentum (12-1 −15.2%, −44% from Aug peak) and volatility (53%); fails a long-only multifactor screen. Quality trajectory (F-score 8/9, accruals −0.118, ROIC quadrupling) and forward multiples argue against a sell. Broken-momentum name: reversal is a trade, not a factor signal.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE. Credit/liquidity risk low (net cash, 55.5x interest cover, survives a −20% revenue stress profitably with ~18x coverage); market risk high (53% vol, −44% max DD, negative Sharpe). Altman Z of 1.53 is a structural false positive — solvency is not the issue.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. Founder holds 57.7% of votes on 16.1% economics; board 43% independent; FPI disclosure regime. Insiders sold at $120–123 (CEO sold ~at the August top) and **zero open-market insider buys through a 54% drawdown** — the single highest-signal governance tell in the file.
- **ESG**: AVERAGE/NEUTRAL. E immaterial (low-carbon, no transition/CBAM exposure); S is the real exposure — responsible lending, gig labor, and merchant commission caps (Indonesia's Oct-2026 six-month rollback is a revenue line, not an ESG footnote); G weak. Apply a structural 5–10% holdco/governance discount.
- **Alternative Data**: NEUTRAL — bullish revenue, bearish margin. Indonesia Shopee search +8% YoY, SPayLater +35%, web traffic +24% MoM, Temu flat — no demand break or visible share loss; the de-rating is a margin/multiple event. **Crack: Brazil search interest −25% YoY and falling into Q4** — the geography consensus leans on for the 25% GMV guide.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: SHORT, moderate conviction — explicitly *not* a fraud short (Beneish −2.79, DSRI 1.01, clean accruals). The case: provisions compounding faster than the book for three quarters, margins compressing despite +43% revenue, Garena decelerating to +5.9% bookings, and consensus FY27 EPS requiring margin expansion into an untested credit cycle. Kill-switch: two quarters of provision growth below book growth.

**Bull Case**
- Valuation has collapsed to 1.18x EV/sales and ~16x FY27E EPS for a 40%+ grower with net cash — scenario-weighted EV ≈ +17%, with a December FOMC pause worth +30–45% on a 1.56-beta de-rated name.
- Monetisation is proving out: take-rate and ads driving gross profit (+51%) faster than revenue (+43%); Shopee EBITDA/GMV expanding (0.58% → 0.68%) even while defending share; alt data shows the demand franchise intact.
- Sum-of-the-parts optionality: a Monee IPO crystallises value buried in a conglomerate multiple; Garena's $458M/quarter EBITDA annuity plus $2B of buyback authorization underpin the downside.

**Bear Case**
- The credit book is the equity: $12.6B of EM consumer loans ≈ book equity, provisions accelerating (+82% YoY) past originations (+59%), NPL90+ drifting 1.1% → 1.3%, and the loss curve has never been tested through a downturn.
- Margin sacrifice is structural, not cyclical: SG&A doubled (34.9% of revenue), Shopee EBITDA −31% YoY, FY26 guidance implies flat-to-down margin — and Garena (the cross-subsidy) is stalling at +5.9% bookings.
- Governance offers no ally: controlling founder, weak board, insiders selling into strength with zero buying at multi-year lows, plus an undisciplined Sea Cloud AI capex venture layered onto a margin-compression cycle.

**Key Risks**
1. Credit-cycle break in Indonesia/Brazil — provisions normalising at the Q3 run-rate (~$2.7B/yr) stalls FY27 earnings growth and forces a re-rating of the entire fintech thesis.
2. Macro binary — a hawkish 9 Dec FOMC plus IDR breaking 19,000 compresses the stock toward $55–60 regardless of operations (the 20 Oct −14% tape is the preview).
3. TikTok Shop share attack converting Shopee's margin expansion into permanent subsidy spend; Brazil deceleration (alt-data flagged) undercutting the 25% GMV guide at the 2 Mar 2027 print.
4. Sovereign removal/commission-cap risk in Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Taiwan; Sea Cloud capex overreach.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Initiate **0.75% starter (band 0.5–1.0%)** — sized so the bear case costs −0.19% of portfolio. Tranche plan: 0.40% now (limit ≤$75) to own the pre-FOMC convexity; +0.35% on 10 Dec only if the FOMC is dovish *or* SE holds >$68 on a hawkish outcome; scale to 2.0–2.5% only after the Q4 print confirms Shopee EBITDA ≥$250M, GMV ≥25%, and provision growth ≤ book growth. Backstop stop: weekly close below $57.50. Exit on any two fundamental invalidation triggers (provision growth > book growth for six straight quarters, NPL90+ >2.0%, Shopee EBITDA <$100M for two quarters, Garena bookings negative, statutory Indonesian commission cap, independent director resignation). Treat SE as EM-internet/EM-credit exposure, not Specialty Retail — fund it by trimming the lowest-conviction EM-internet holding (correlation to MELI 0.45), and add no other EM-fintech credit risk while held.

**Agent disagreement flags**: ROIC (19.2% vs 11.7%) and net cash ($9.5B vs $3.1B) differ by loan-book capital treatment — this memo adopts the conservative figures. Growth (BUY) vs Short (SHORT) vs Value (PASS) is resolved by the strategist's scenario EV (+17%) and starter sizing. Sell-side targets ($105–135 median) are stale and being cut; do not anchor to them. Peer multiples were not retrievable; the valuation case rests on SE's own history and the DCF.

# PORTFOLIO CONSTRUCTION RECOMMENDATION — SEA LIMITED (NYSE: SE)

**Price anchor (verified): $73.44, 12-Nov-2026** | Mkt cap $44.9–46.9B (definitional gap, see §8) | GICS: Consumer Cyclical / Specialty Retail (artifact — true exposure is EM internet + EM consumer credit + mobile gaming)

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Growth Researcher** | **BUY** (not Strong) | Medium-High | LTM rev +44.1%, GM 45.9%, Rule of 40 = 56, 1.18x EV/FY26E sales — cheapest SE has ever traded vs growth. Withholds Strong Buy until Shopee EBITDA re-inflects >$269M |
| **Short Analyst** | **SHORT** | Medium | Provisions +65%→+72%→+82% vs loan book +59% — three consecutive quarters of deteriorating loss rate per unit lent. Q3 provision ($682M) exceeds group operating income ($640M). **Not a fraud short** (Beneish −2.79, clean DSRI) |

| **Non-Financial Risk** | **HIGH risk** | High | 57.7% voting on 16.1% economics; 3 of 7 board independent; ~40 Form 4s in 60 days (mostly sales) and **zero insider open-market buys through a 54% drawdown** |

| **Alt Data** | **NEUTRAL** (bullish revenue / bearish margin) | Medium | ID Shopee search +8%, SPayLater +35%, traffic +24% MoM, Temu flat — no share-loss visible. **But Brazil interest −25% YoY and falling**: the geography consensus leans on is decelerating into Q4 |
| **Geo Legal** | **MEDIUM** | Medium | No sanctions, no DOJ/SEC action, $46M class action settled. But regulatory intensity in the core *profit* pools (Indonesia, Brazil, Vietnam, Taiwan) is high and rising; Free Fire India ban is the proven removal template |
| **ESG** | **AVERAGE / NEUTRAL** | Medium | Low-carbon (E immaterial), High social, weak G. Merchant commission caps and OJK rate ceilings are **revenue lines, not ESG factors**. Apply a 5–10% structural holdco/governance discount |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **MEDIUM agreement, SPLIT on direction**

**Universal agreement (high confidence, all 11 agents):** SE is a genuinely high-quality operating business with an accelerating top line, a fortress net-cash balance sheet, and no fraud. Not one agent — including the short — disputes the fundamentals or alleges accounting manipulation. That is a strong, cross-validated floor.

**The split is narrow and specific:** Growth says buy the growth at 1.2x sales; Value says the growth is not yet worth the price; Short says the *credit book* will force the margin question sooner than consensus expects. Macro says the discount rate, not the business, is setting the price.

**Conflict resolution:**
1. **No fraud override applies.** The framework's "fraud risk takes precedence" rule was tested and does *not* trigger — Beneish −2.79, accruals −11.8%, DSRI 1.01, clean SEC record. The Short's case is therefore a **weighted fundamental risk**, not a veto.
2. **I resolve the ROIC/cash-flow conflict against the bulls.** Sector cited 19.2% ROIC and ~10x EV/FCF; Value and Short independently derived 11.7% ROIC and ~4% owner-earnings yield. The difference is the fintech loan book, which consumes shareholder capital without appearing in FCF. The conservative figures govern: **ROIC ≈ WACC, owner-earnings yield ≈ 3.2–4%.** This alone caps sizing.
3. **I discount the sell-side.** Median target is still ~$110–133, but the *direction* is unambiguous — Barclays $156→(cut), Morgan Stanley $153→$121→, BofA →$110, New Street downgraded to Neutral at **$70**. Price-target momentum is a contrarian indicator here; do not treat $110 as fair value.
4. **Alt data resolves the "demand vs margin" question in favour of margin.** Revenue is fine (indeed beating); the de-rating is a multiple/margin event. That supports a *small* position, not a large one — because margin is the variable we cannot observe and the Short's provision trend hits exactly there.

**Net aggregated conviction: MEDIUM-LOW, positive expected value, wide dispersion.** This is not a 3–5% position under any framework.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation

### **0.75% of portfolio — starter position only (band 0.5–1.0%)**

**Scenario-weighted intrinsic value:**

| Scenario | Prob. | Price | Contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bear — TikTok share gains, provisions normalise at Q3 run-rate, cloud capex drag | 30% | $55 | $16.5 |
| Base — Shopee holds share, margin flat, Monee grows into its loss rate | 45% | $85 | $38.3 |
| Bull — credit benign, Shopee EBITDA re-inflects, Monee IPO crystallises SOTP | 25% | $125 | $31.3 |
| **Expected value** | | **≈$86** | **+17% vs $73.44** |

Positive EV — but the distribution spans $55 to $135 (a 1.5x range), and my scenario weights carry an honest ±15pp standard error. Unconstrained Kelly on these inputs returns ~35–40%, which is **model noise, not a signal**, because the dominant error term is estimation uncertainty in the credit loss rate — the one input no agent could observe. Taking a disciplined fraction (~1/40th) lands at 0.75–1.0%, which independently matches the firm's rule for *"low conviction or multiple risk flags → 0.5–1%."*

**Why not larger:** only ~12% discount to intrinsic value vs a 25–30% requirement (Value); momentum is the worst in the peer group and factor discipline says wait for inflection (Quant); provisions have outrun the loan book three quarters running with an untested loss curve (Short); a 43%-independent board with zero insider buying gives us no informational ally (Non-Fin); and the 9-Dec FOMC is a coin-flip binary layered on a name that fell 14% in one day on a bond-market move (Macro).

**Why not zero:** the business is not deteriorating — revenue beat by 6.3%, gross margin expanded to 45.9%, and 90% of SE's variance is idiosyncratic (R² vs SPY = 0.10), so even a 1% position adds trivially to portfolio risk while carrying meaningful upside optionality.

**Risk contribution:** 0.75% × 53% vol = **0.40% portfolio vol**; beta-equivalent exposure 1.17%. Loss at the bear case (−25%) = **−0.19% of portfolio.** The position is sized so that being completely wrong is immaterial.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector:** Treat SE as **EM internet / EM consumer fintech**, not Specialty Retail. Establish or respect a house sleeve cap (~6–8%) for global EM internet. If that sleeve already holds MELI, CPNG or PDD, **fund SE by trimming the lowest-conviction holding rather than adding incrementally** — SE is a substitution into a contested sub-sector, not a new source of diversification within it.

**Correlation (252d, verified):**

| | MELI | SPY | PDD | CPNG | BABA | EEM | AMZN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SE** | **0.45** | 0.31 | 0.28 | 0.28 | 0.28 | 0.26 | 0.23 |

SE's highest correlation is MELI (0.45) — the same LatAm e-commerce/fintech story. Correlation to EEM is only 0.26, so SE is *not* a cheap EM beta proxy; it is a single-name bet. **Combined with R² of 0.10 vs SPY, this is a stock-specific/event-risk allocation, not a factor allocation** — so the binding constraint is an *event-risk budget* (Q4 print, Monee IPO, FOMC), not a factor budget.

**Factor exposure added:** negative momentum, high volatility, high beta, long duration, EM FX translation. It does **not** add genuine value (P/FCF 10.4x is inflated by loan-book float; owner-earnings yield is ~3.5% on a 4.2% 10Y — no value cushion). If the book is already long duration/EM, SE **compounds** existing exposure to USD strength and IDR — and the 9-Dec FOMC hits the whole book simultaneously. That is a portfolio-level reason to stay at the low end of the band.

**Concentration risks to monitor:** (a) Monee's $12.6B loan book ≈ 1:1 with book equity — a 10% stress loss ≈ 80% of FY26E net income; (b) Garena is ~54% of segment profit growth and is expropriable by decree (India 2022 precedent); (c) 57.7% voting control removes any activist or takeover floor.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in on three tranches — do not buy in one clip**

The tape argues for patience: the 10-Nov earnings day printed **19.5M shares** (opened $79.75, high $85.16, closed $76.80 — a violent intraday fade) followed by 11.7M shares down. The 12-Nov close of $73.44 came on just **2.9M shares** — light-volume drift, not capitulation volume. No seller exhaustion yet.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — now** | 0.40% | At market, limit ≤$75 | Owns the pre-FOMC convexity Macro identified (Dec pause ≈ 10:1 asymmetric, +30–45%) at 1.2x EV/sales |
| **T2 — 10 Dec** | 0.35% | Either a dovish 9-Dec FOMC outcome, **or** a hawkish outcome with SE holding >$68 | Removes the binary; if hike-and-hawkish breaks $68 the thesis is losing the multiple argument — do not average into it |
| **T3 — 3 Mar 2027** | +0.7–1.2% | Post-Q4 print: Shopee adj. EBITDA ≥$250M **and** GMV ≥25% **and** provision growth ≤ loan-book growth | Converts the position from macro trade to fundamental hold. Max total 2.0–2.5% |

**Execution rules:** use limit orders only; never add within 5 sessions either side of an earnings date (10-Nov gapped 8% and reversed 10% intraday); ADTV ~7M shares (~$500M) means a 0.75% position is liquid to exit in under a day at <10% of ADV — no liquidity concession required.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Primary exit is fundamental, not price** — a 53%-vol name generates ±15% monthly 2σ moves, so a tight price stop is guaranteed to be noise-triggered.

**Thesis invalidation — exit on any TWO:**
1. Provisions grow faster than the loan book for three more consecutive quarters (six total), or NPL90+ exceeds **2.0%**.
2. Shopee adj. EBITDA below **$100M** for two consecutive quarters (Growth's own sell trigger).
3. Garena bookings growth turns negative, or QAU declines >5% QoQ.
4. FY2027 guidance implies group EBITDA margin below FY2026 with the $1B Shopee target abandoned.
5. Sea Cloud AI annual capex commitment >$1.5B with no disclosed contracted customer revenue.
6. **Statutory** (not voluntary) Indonesian merchant commission cap, any adverse KPPU ruling, or capital-control/repatriation measures.
7. Any independent director resignation (the single highest-signal governance event at a 43%-independent board).

**Price stop (backstop only):** weekly close below **$57.50** (−22%). Set beyond the 2σ monthly band *and* at the top of the bear case ($50–58), so it fires only if the fundamental case has already broken.

**Trim triggers:** sell ⅓ at **$100** (~1.2x central IV), ⅓ at **$115** (floor of the bull case), let the residual run behind a 20% trailing stop. Mechanical rebalance if the position exceeds **3.0%** of portfolio through appreciation.

**Portfolio-level overlays:** (a) halve the position ahead of the 9-Dec FOMC if the book's aggregate duration is already high; (b) no additional EM-fintech credit exposure while SE is held; (c) monitor USD/IDR (18,230), USD/BRL (5.49), and the Monee provision line as the three leading indicators — each is a direct input to the exit rules above.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — starter position, 0.75% (band 0.5–1.0%)**

Not "Add." Not a 3–5% conviction position. The aggregate read across eleven specialists is an **excellent operator, fairly-to-mildly-cheaply priced, with one unresolved and unfalsifiable risk (the credit loss rate) and a hostile macro tape.** That combination earns a seat in the book at a size that costs nothing if wrong and matters if right — plus a pre-committed path to 2.0–2.5% only on evidence.

**What would move me to a full 3% position:** an FOMC pause *and* two consecutive quarters of provision growth decelerating below loan-book growth *and* Shopee EBITDA back above $250M. **What would move me to Pass/Exit:** any two invalidation triggers, or a decisive break of $57.50.

---

## 8. Data Gaps & Reconciliation Notes

- **Market cap:** tool computes $46.9B (638.2M diluted × $73.44); agents used $44.9B (~basic). Sizing unaffected; both are below the $50B+ implied by stale targets.
- **Net cash:** reported variously as $9.46B (Fin Risk), $4.66B (Sector), $3.05B (Short). I used **$3.05B** — the equity-relevant figure after haircutting cash that funds the loan book. All three imply no solvency risk, which is the only conclusion that matters here.
- **ROIC:** 19.2% (Sector) vs 11.7% (Value/Quant). Used the conservative figure; the gap is loan-book capital.
- **Beta:** 1.16 (252d daily) vs 1.56 (profile/5yr). Used 1.16 for short-horizon risk, 1.56 for cost of equity.
- **Not retrievable:** SE 20-F risk factors (FPI, tool 403), peer valuation multiples (BABA/PDD outputs non-credible), patent/Indeed quantitative feeds. GMV share figures are third-party estimates (Momentum Works via secondary sources); HHI is derived. Next earnings date (~2-Mar-2027) is derived from reporting cadence, not a confirmed calendar entry.

# Sector Brief: Sea Limited (SE) — Emerging-Market E-Commerce, Fintech & Gaming

**Note on classification:** FMP tags SE as *Consumer Cyclical / Specialty Retail*, which is a GICS artifact. Its true competitive set is EM internet platforms (Shopee vs TikTok Shop/Tokopedia, Lazada; Monee vs MELI's fintech arm, GoTo; Garena vs global mobile gaming). I benchmark against both the reported peer list and the true comp set. Price/date anchor: **$73.10, 12 Nov 2026**; market cap $44.8B, EV $40.1B.

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Southeast Asian e-commerce is a **highly concentrated, late-growth oligopoly**: Shopee (~53% of regional platform GMV, ~$83B in 2025), TikTok Shop incl. Tokopedia (~29%, $45.6B) and Lazada (~17%) together hold **98.8% of platform GMV**, implying a rough HHI of ~3,900 — concentrated by any antitrust standard. The pool is still expanding: SEA digital-economy e-commerce GMV ran ~$159B in 2024 and is forecast at ~$226B in 2026 (~19% CAGR), with penetration still well below China. The sector's economics are shifting from *subsidy-funded GMV land-grab* to *monetisation* — take rates, advertising and credit attach — which is why Sea's revenue is growing (43% YoY in Q3 2026) faster than GMV. But that transition is being contested: TikTok's entry from $4.4B (2022) to $45.6B (2025) SEA GMV has re-ignited spend competition precisely as investors demand margin proof.

**Cycle position: mid-to-late growth.** Volume growth is decelerating to the high-teens/25% range while monetisation still compounds — the classic "margin-proof" phase. The adjacent consumer-credit cycle is mid-expansion and showing first strain (Monee's EBITDA margin fell 26.5% → 18.6% as its loan book grew 60%).

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Structural GMV runway + LatAm optionality.** SEA e-commerce ~$159B (2024) → ~$226B (2026E). Shopee did **$39.7B GMV in Q3 2026 alone** with adj. EBITDA at 0.68% of GMV (up from 0.58%), and Brazil adds a second under-penetrated TAM.
- **Monetisation mix shift is real.** Q3 2026 gross profit rose **+51.4% vs revenue +43.4%**, i.e. margin pressure sits in opex and credit cost, not in the transaction take rate. Ads + commission expansion is the structural margin lever, and Shopee's ~0.7% EBITDA/GMV remains far below mature-platform levels.
- **Self-funding cash machine.** Garena throws off $458M quarterly adj. EBITDA (~55% margin) on a 671.7M QAU / 68.6M paying-user base, funding Shopee's fight; group holds **$9.5B gross cash, $4.66B net cash**, ROIC 19.2%, EV/FCF ~10x.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **TikTok Shop/Tokopedia share attack.** From $4.4B to $45.6B SEA GMV in three years. Sea's Q4-25 print (3 Mar 2026) missed on competition and the stock fell **-17% in a day** (intraday as much as -27%); a DBS downgrade on 20 Oct 2026 (margin, FX, competition) took another -9%.
- **Margin compression across the group.** Q3 2026 adj. EBITDA margin **12.1% → 10.8%**; Monee EBITDA margin **26.5% → 18.6%** on a $12.6B loan book (+60%) as provisions front-load; FY26 Shopee guidance of ~$1B adj. EBITDA on ~25% GMV growth implies **flat-to-down margin**. Effective tax rate jumped to 34.5% ($280M vs $161M).
- **FX/energy and LatAm cash burn.** Weakening IDR/THB/BRL and energy costs hit SEA consumer wallets; gross cash fell $10.5B → $9.5B YoY. In Brazil it faces MELI growing 39% at 44.5% GM / 11.1% OM.

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

Latest reported fiscal year (SE FY25; BABA FY-Mar-26; others FY25). Revenue growth is latest FY YoY.

| Company | Revenue | Rev growth | Gross margin | Operating margin | 3-yr growth trend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sea (SE)** | $22.9B | **+36.4%** | 44.7% | 8.1% | 4.9% → 28.8% → 36.4% (**re-accelerating**) |
| Amazon (AMZN) | $716.9B | +12.4% | 50.3% | 11.2% | 9.4 → 11.8 → 11.0 → 12.4 (steady) |
| Alibaba (BABA) | ¥1,023.7B | +2.7% | 39.8% | 5.8% | 1.8 → 8.3 → 5.9 → 2.7 (stalling) |
| PDD | ¥431.8B | +9.7% | 56.3% | 21.6% | 39.0 → 89.7 → 59.0 → 9.7 (**sharp slowdown**) |
| MercadoLibre (MELI) | $28.9B | +39.1% | 44.5% | 11.1% | 52.5 → 40.1 → 37.5 → 39.1 (durable) |
| Coupang (CPNG) | $34.5B | +14.1% | 29.4% | 1.4% | 11.8 → 18.5 → 24.1 → 14.1 |
| **Peer median (ex-SE)** | — | **+12.4%** | **44.5%** | **11.1%** | — |

**Read-through:** SE grows at **2.9x the peer median** and its gross margin is exactly at the median (44.7% vs 44.5%) — a genuinely rare combination.
